question: Will Russia and Ukraine both publicly confirm a mutual energy-infrastructure ceasefire agreement by October 3, 2026?

calls.reasoning: Status quo is no agreement, and the question needs BOTH governments to confirm a reciprocal halt during a 3-day window 9-11 days out. Reference class of US-brokered partial wartime truces jointly confirmed within a ~2-week window is a few percent; the March 2025 and January 2026 episodes show the mechanism can fire fast under Trump pressure, which lifts the number above pure base rate. Against: Peskov's stated price includes lifting energy-export sanctions and stopping tanker strikes, unreachable by Oct 3; the Kremlin said on Sept 10 there were no substantive talks; FT reporting and Ukrainian analysts say Putin wants to keep the option of a mid-to-late-October grid campaign; both sides struck each other through Sept 21-22. Russia is not present at the Sept 22 New York meeting, so the most likely bullish outcome is a Ukrainian/US announcement that Moscow does not mirror - which the fine print explicitly excludes. Evidence is one-sided toward NO, so I stay near the low base rate with a modest bump for live diplomacy.
calls.reference_class: US-brokered partial (domain-limited) ceasefires in active interstate wars where both belligerents publicly confirm a reciprocal halt within ~2 weeks of negotiations starting, while each attaches non-overlapping preconditions
